8. Can two vectors spanallofR3? Can three vectors spanR3andat the same time
be dependent? Explain through ”new directions.”
[Source: TA Problems, Week 1, Problem 8]
Solution.
Two vectors span at most a plane — each vector gives at most one
new direction, and two directions cannot fill three-dimensional space. Three de-
pendent vectors also span at most a plane: dependence means one of them is a
combination of the others and does not add a third direction. To achieve R3, three
independent directions are needed; therefore, three dependent vectors will never
spanR3.

rank(B)for any compatible B.
[Source: LA Practice Week 4, Problem 10]
Solution. Multiplication by an invertible matrix does not change the number of
pivots: standard reasoning: rank(AB) ≤rankB (rows of AB are combinations of
rows of B), and applying the same to B = A−1(AB), we get rankB ≤rank(AB); both
inequalities force equality. Intuition: an invertible factor only stretches/rotates/
shifts spaces, but does not flatten them, so rank cannot be lost or gained.
